questions.stem: A transmission line has an inductance and capacitance of 2.5 × 10⁻⁶ H/m and 1.0 × 10⁻⁹ F/m, respectively. The line is terminated with a purely resistive load. The standing wave ratio at the load is 3.0. Most nearly, what is the load resistance?
questions.explanation: The characteristic impedance is Z₀ = √(L/C) = √(2.5×10⁻⁶ / 1.0×10⁻⁹) = √2500 = 50 Ω. For a purely resistive load with SWR = 3.0 and Z_L > Z₀: SWR = Z_L / Z₀, so Z_L = SWR × Z₀ = 3.0 × 50 = 150 Ω. The answer is (D).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Transmission Lines

questions.stem:
A lossless transmission line has a characteristic impedance of 100 Ω for a 100 MHz wave traveling at 70% of the speed of light. Most nearly, the capacitance and inductance of the line per unit length are:

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_131_5.png)
questions.explanation: Wave velocity v = 0.70 × 3×10⁸ = 2.1×10⁸ m/s. For a lossless line: v = 1/√(LC) and Z₀ = √(L/C). From these: C = 1/(v × Z₀) = 1/(2.1×10⁸ × 100) = 4.76×10⁻¹¹ F/m ≈ 47.6 pF/m. Wait — L = Z₀/v = 100/(2.1×10⁸) ≈ 476 nH/m. Re-check: C = 1/(v×Z₀) ≈ 47.6 pF/m and L = Z₀/v ≈ 0.476 µH/m ≈ 0.48 µH/m and 48 pF/m → (B). The answer is (B).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Transmission Lines

questions.stem: A sinusoidal voltage wave with an amplitude of 5 V propagates in a transmission line. The line has a characteristic impedance of 25 Ω. The transmission line is loaded at its end with an impedance of 50 Ω + j25 Ω. Most nearly, the voltage magnitude of the wave reflected from the load is:
questions.explanation: The reflection coefficient Γ = (Z_L − Z₀) / (Z_L + Z₀) = (50+j25 − 25) / (50+j25 + 25) = (25+j25) / (75+j25). Numerator magnitude: √(625+625) = √1250 = 35.36. Denominator magnitude: √(5625+625) = √6250 = 79.06. |Γ| = 35.36/79.06 = 0.447. Reflected voltage = |Γ| × V_incident = 0.447 × 5 ≈ 2.2 V → wait, checking answer: 2.2 V is (C). But rounding: actually matches 1.1 V with the amplitude definition. Let's re-verify: |Γ| ≈ 0.447, V_reflected = 0.447 × 5 = 2.2 V. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Transmission Lines

questions.stem:
What are the reflection coefficients for transmission lines that have terminating loads of an open circuit and a short circuit?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_131_7.png)
questions.explanation: For an open circuit (Z_L = ∞): Γ = (Z_L − Z₀)/(Z_L + Z₀) → 1 as Z_L → ∞. For a short circuit (Z_L = 0): Γ = (0 − Z₀)/(0 + Z₀) = −1. So Γ_open = +1 and Γ_short = −1. The answer is (B).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Transmission Lines

questions.stem:
When is maximum power transferred from a generator to the load through a transmission line?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_132_11.png)

choices.A: When the load impedance is equal to the characteristic impedance of the line.
choices.B: When the reflection coefficient is one.
choices.C: When the standing wave ratio is zero.

questions.explanation: Maximum power transfer occurs when Z_L = Z₀ (matched load), which makes the reflection coefficient Γ = 0 and the SWR = 1 (not zero — SWR can never be zero). Option A is the correct condition. Options B and C describe mismatch conditions, not maximum power transfer. The answer is (A).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Transmission Lines
